title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
summary: Given two arrays of positive integers, arr1 and arr2, find the length of the longest common prefix between any integer in arr1 and any integer in arr2.
statement: Given two arrays of positive integers, arr1 and arr2, find the length of the longest common prefix between any integer in arr1 and any integer in arr2. A common prefix is an integer formed by the shared starting digits of two numbers. Return the length of the longest such prefix, or 0 if no common prefix exists.
constraints: Both arrays are nonempty and contain positive integers.
A prefix consists of one or more leading decimal digits.
Return the maximum common-prefix length across one number from each array, or zero.
hints: Removing trailing decimal digits enumerates every nonempty prefix of an integer.
Store all prefixes from the first array, then shorten each second-array value until it matches one.
Repeatedly divide by ten; on the first stored match update the maximum digit length.
The first match while shortening is the longest for that pair, and checking every second-array number covers all cross-array pairs.
editorial: The first match while shortening is the longest for that pair, and checking every second-array number covers all cross-array pairs.

tests.explanation: The pair one hundred and one thousand shares prefix 100 of length three.
No cross-array pair shares even its first digit, so the result is zero.
